title: Changelog - November 12, 2026
summary: This week's Corgea changelog adds Scala support, private container registry scanning, and configurable revalidation for earlier findings.
body_markdown:
This week’s roundup covers public Corgea releases from November 5 through November 11, 2026. The updates add Scala support, let container scans use private registry credentials, and give teams a more reliable way to track findings across scans.


## Top 3 features


### 1. Scala support for code scanning


Corgea now scans Scala source files (` .scala


`


) and scripts (` .sc


`


). Scala is also supported by Maven private package registries, so teams can include internal Scala dependencies in their dependency analysis.


### 2. Private registry credentials for container scans


Container scans can now pull images from private Docker registries. Teams can configure registry credentials for every project or limit them to selected projects. Corgea matches credentials by registry host, so one Docker or OCI registry entry can cover the images on that host.


### 3. Revalidation for earlier findings


When revalidation is enabled, full and pull request scans recheck earlier SAST findings that a new scan does not report again. Findings stay in the new results when Corgea confirms they are still present, and their existing triage remains in place if a valid verdict is unavailable. This prevents a finding from appearing fixed simply because a recheck was inconclusive.


## More features and improvements


- Advanced Vulnerability Search now displays policy titles and can search full policy descriptions.
- GitHub draft pull requests skip scans, comments, and Corgea Agent replies until they are ready for review. Company admins can opt in to draft scanning and commenting from PR Rules.
- Workbench grouped results and the triage approvals queue are faster for organizations with large result sets.
- Carried-forward findings now show the current scan’s file content and revalidation reasoning. Fixes generated for a different file version are no longer reused.
- Identical concurrent CLI uploads for the same commit and scan settings share one scan instead of duplicating work in CI.
- The built-in Admin role can no longer be deleted.
- Reviewers can undo an applied triage approval when the finding has not changed, restoring its earlier status, comment, and accepted-risk expiry.
- Notification emails include unsubscribe links for their notification type. SLA violation emails now follow email preferences.
- Reports can use a configurable query time limit, with a 90-second default for on-premises installations.
- Workbench exports default to selected findings when there is a selection.
- Dependencies exports filtered by project and reachability are faster.
- Linear tickets can now be created for pentest findings, with links retained across runs of the same finding.
- New projects uploaded through the web interface can be tagged before their first scan.
- Reporting filters for projects and teams load options as users search and scroll.
- Policy Center loading, filtering, and status changes are faster, and Dependencies inventory browsing is faster for organizations with extensive scan histories.
- Developer Insights follows the Reporting filter bar and refreshes with reporting data.
- Code Vulnerabilities reports show progress during updates, preserve earlier results when available, and provide retry or narrower-filter guidance.
- Scan CSV exports include first-detection dates and occurrence counts for older findings.
- Corgea Agent avoids unrelated pull request threads while continuing conversations in threads it has joined.
- Reporting tabs keep loading when users switch views, reload when filters change, and provide a Retry action after an error.
- Incremental scans rescan a file when another file that its finding depends on changes.
- Findings exports now use one Export button, start from current filters, build in the background, and remain available in Recent exports for 24 hours.
- CSV exports support up to 150,000 rows by default and report when a request exceeds that limit.
- Triage approval API endpoints are available to list, view, approve, and reject requests with the same access rules as the approvals queue.
- Companies without SSO can use authenticator app sign-in where it is available, with recovery codes and administrator controls.
- Immediate status changes show Reviewing justification while approval is pending.
- Large SARIF exports no longer time out.
- Corgea policy changes beyond descriptions create new policy versions, and invalid instruction types return validation errors.
- Triage suggestions can now check a SAST or SCA false-positive claim against the code before submission. Reviewers can see the result on the approval request.
- Reviewers can use Investigate deeper on pending triage approval requests to have Corgea check the finding against the full repository without running the code.
